channel.title: Pruning My Pothos
channel.description: Practical explainers, field notes, and architectural breakdowns of AI systems, grounded in real use and explained in plain language.

item.title: What Has to Survive for Work to Continue
item.description: Work that spans sessions, people and agents needs more than a record of what happened. It needs what is currently true, and someone who owns the next step.

item.title: AI Agents vs AI Workflows
item.description: The difference is not tool use or sophistication. It is whether your program fixed the sequence in advance or the model gets to choose what happens next.

item.title: How the Parts of an AI Application Depend on Each Other
item.description: The boxes in an architecture diagram are the easy part. What matters is what each part establishes, and what the next part is assuming was already settled.

item.title: When Chat Renders an Interface
item.description: An assistant can render controls instead of sentences. What a rendered card actually tells you, what a button actually means, and where the real decision still happens.

item.title: Context Windows: What the Model Can See in One Run
item.description: A context window is the bounded information available to the model for one run. Why that is not memory, what happens when you reach the limit, and why selection still matters at any size.

item.title: Designing Reusable AI Skills
item.description: Turning a prompt that worked into something reusable means declaring what it takes, what it returns, what it may touch and when it should stop.

item.title: What Counts as Good, and How to Check It
item.description: Evaluation compares behaviour against an expectation someone wrote down first. What to check, which method suits which property, and what keeps a change in behaviour visible.

item.title: From Agent Intent to Governed Execution
item.description: What has to happen between a model asking for an action and that action changing something real, and which layer owns each failure.

item.title: When Is an AI System Ready for Real Use?
item.description: Readiness is a decision about exposure, not a stage a system reaches. What has to be true before you let real users depend on an AI workflow.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop Is a System Design Choice
item.description: Requiring a human decision is easy. Making sure that person can actually decide, with the context, the alternatives and a path after no, is the design work.

item.title: The I-7 Loop: A Working Method for Delegating to AI
item.description: Seven named points where a person decides something before an AI agent acts, and the five-minute version that makes them usable.

item.title: What to Record So You Can Explain What Happened
item.description: Observability is the ability to investigate behaviour from signals a system preserves while it runs. What to keep, what monitoring and audit and replay each mean, and where a record stops being proof.

item.title: Policy-Governed MCP Runtimes: Trust Boundaries for Tool Execution
item.description: When a tool-connected system reads content, that content can contain instructions. What follows for where policy decisions belong, and what isolation can bound.

item.title: Prompting Is Not the Skill You Think It Is
item.description: A prompt can describe what you want. It cannot make the system check it. Why the useful skill is diagnosing output and knowing which requirements have to leave the prompt.

item.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Plain Terms
item.description: Retrieval finds candidate material. Context assembly decides what the model receives. Where those two differ, and why finding the right document is not the same as getting the right answer.

item.title: Why the Loop Outlives the Model
item.description: A note on why much of what a user experiences in an action-taking system comes from the software around the model, and why that software is what survives a model change.

item.title: Semantic Caching: Similar Is Not Safe to Reuse
item.description: A note on reusing answers across differently worded questions, and the one failure that makes it dangerous: two questions can look alike and need opposite answers.

item.title: What a Publisher Actually Controls
item.description: SEO, AEO and GEO mostly describe someone else's system. The publishing controls you hold are a short list, and every one of them can be checked.

item.title: Prompt, Skill, Workflow, Agent: Telling the Layers Apart
item.description: These words name different responsibilities, not stages of sophistication. What each one covers, and how to tell which you are looking at.

item.title: Structured Output and Why It Matters
item.description: A schema gives software something it can check. What each layer of checking actually establishes, and what valid output still does not tell you.

item.title: What Systems Thinking Helps You Inspect
item.description: A handful of old ideas that still earn their place when looking at an AI system: where the boundaries are, what the feedback does, and three ways things go wrong quietly.

item.title: The Instruction Spec: Defining an AI-Assisted Software Change
item.description: Six fields written down before an agent touches the code, and a risk category that decides which approvals the change needs.

item.title: Tool Use: When Language Triggers Actions
item.description: A model does not call a tool. It produces a request, and ordinary software decides whether that request becomes an action.

item.title: What a System Prompt Actually Is
item.description: A system prompt sets the conditions an interaction runs under. What belongs in one, what does not, and why it influences behaviour without enforcing anything.

item.title: Why OCR Quietly Breaks Document AI
item.description: OCR sits at the front of every document pipeline. When it misreads a table or a total, every retrieval step and every answer downstream inherits that error.

item.title: From Text to Tokens
item.description: Models do not read words. They read a sequence of integers produced by a tokenizer. What that step does, and why token counts behave differently from character counts.

item.title: Training, Fine-Tuning, and Inference
item.description: What changes the model itself, and what only changes what the model sees during one run. The distinction that decides whether you need training or better context.

item.title: What an AI Model Actually Is
item.description: A trained model is a file of learned numbers that turns input into likely continuations. What that file does on its own, and what the software around it has to supply.

item.title: Debugging a Semantic Cache Miss
item.description: A reflective look at debugging a user-facing issue where a semantic cache returned a stale context block due to a loose similarity threshold.

item.title: Debugging My First Schema Translation Error
item.description: A reflection on how a minor change in structured output syntax broke our downstream processing.

item.title: What I Learned Debugging a Multi-Agent System
item.description: The debugging session that taught me why observability is not optional in orchestration, and what I now look for first when a multi-agent system misbehaves.

item.title: Designing My First Safety Constraint
item.description: What I learned designing the first architectural boundary in an autonomous system, and why I had to resist the urge to make it configurable.

item.title: Learning to Say I Don't Know
item.description: What I learned about trust and reliability when I started designing systems that acknowledged the limits of their own reasoning.

item.title: What I Learned Running AI Governance at Scale
item.description: What I discovered when governance contracts met real organizational behavior, and why the blueprint rarely survives first contact with the workflow.

item.title: How I Run a Weekly Eval Loop
item.description: A small review ritual for checking whether my AI workflows are getting clearer or only getting faster.

item.title: Building a Knowledge Surface
item.description: How I moved from collecting notes to designing a usable memory surface for writing and AI workflows.

item.title: Decision Logs Beat Memory
item.description: Why I now log decision rationale instead of trusting recall when AI workflows become ambiguous.

item.title: The Weekly Observability Reset
item.description: A small weekly ritual that keeps my AI workflows honest after launch.

item.title: Writing for Two Readers
item.description: How I now write for both humans and retrieval systems without flattening voice.

item.title: Unfinished Questions
item.description: The questions you keep open shape the person you become.

item.title: The Second Voice
item.description: A quieter perspective that keeps the first from taking over.

item.title: Margin of Error
item.description: Why you need slack if you want consistency.

item.title: Learning Edges
item.description: The boundary between comfort and growth is where progress hides.

item.title: The Inner Critic, Rewritten
item.description: Turn the sharp voice into a useful editor.

item.title: Habit as Identity
item.description: The small act that becomes a quiet biography.

item.title: Friction Forecast
item.description: Predicting where you will stumble saves the day.

item.title: Edit Your Environment
item.description: Change the room and the mind follows.

item.title: Doubt as a Tool
item.description: How uncertainty sharpens choices instead of slowing them.

item.title: The Craft of Saying No
item.description: Refusal as a creative act, not a closed door.

item.title: Constraint of Kindness
item.description: Limits that protect energy and keep the work human.

item.title: Calibration Rituals
item.description: Small rituals that reset the mind before the day drifts.

item.title: Attention Debt
item.description: What you borrow from your focus now gets repaid with anxiety later.

item.title: D.I.Y.
item.description: A quiet rebellion: fixing small things to build a steadier self.

item.title: My First Thought
item.description: Why the second thought deserves more of the spotlight.
